rule.title: Pass the Hash Activity 2
rule.author: Dave Kennedy, Jeff Warren (method) / David Vassallo (rule)

es.summary: Se registró un inicio de sesión exitoso (4624) con un patrón asociado a Pass the Hash: una sesión de red NTLM con KeyLength 0 o una sesión de tipo 9 (NewCredentials) creada por seclogo.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 4624 que cumplen alguna de dos condiciones: LogonType 3 con LogonProcessName NtLmSsp, SubjectUserSid S-1-0-0 y KeyLength 0; o LogonType 9 con LogonProcessName seclogo. Se excluye TargetUserName ANONYMOUS LOGON.
es.why_it_matters: Con Pass the Hash (ATT&CK T1550.002) el atacante se autentica con el hash NTLM robado, sin conocer la contraseña, y se mueve lateralmente. Las herramientas que inyectan hashes suelen generar sesiones de tipo 9 con seclogo.
triage_steps: Identifique la variante: LogonType 3 (sesión entrante en el host destino) o LogonType 9 (sesión NewCredentials en el host de origen).
En LogonType 3, revise TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, IpAddress y WorkstationName. Confirme que el equipo de origen y la cuenta suelen relacionarse.
En LogonType 9, revise SubjectUserName, TargetOutboundUserName y ProcessName. Determine si alguien usó runas /netonly a propósito o si las credenciales se inyectaron.
En el origen, busque en 4688 o Sysmon, +/- 15 minutos, runas.exe, herramientas de volcado de credenciales y accesos a lsass.exe (Sysmon 10).
En el destino, correlacione con el mismo TargetLogonId: 4672 (privilegios especiales), 5140/5145 (recursos compartidos), 7045 (servicios nuevos) y 4688.
Pivotee por la cuenta y por IpAddress para ver si hay inicios de sesión NTLM en varios hosts o fallos 4625 previos.
Revise alertas anteriores de la misma cuenta y del mismo host, y valide con el responsable si había una tarea administrativa autorizada.
false_positives: Administradores que usan runas /netonly o consolas de gestión con credenciales alternativas (LogonType 9).
Herramientas de inventario, monitoreo o despliegue que se autentican por NTLM contra muchos equipos.
Aplicaciones o servicios heredados que solo usan NTLM y generan sesiones de red con KeyLength 0.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño de la cuenta y con el área de TI si la actividad era legítima antes de actuar.
Si es maliciosa, aísle el host de origen desde el EDR y restrinja la cuenta afectada.
Restablezca la contraseña de la cuenta comprometida y de las cuentas privilegiadas que tuvieron sesión en el origen, e invalide sus sesiones activas.
Busque persistencia y movimiento lateral en los hosts destino (servicios, tareas programadas, binarios nuevos) y elimínelos después de preservar la evidencia.
Para reducir la superficie, limite NTLM, use LAPS, agregue las cuentas privilegiadas a Protected Users y active Credential Guard.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel medio es adecuado porque el patrón coincide con Pass the Hash, pero runas /netonly y NTLM legítimo también lo generan, así que hay que confirmarlo con contexto.

en.summary: A successful logon (4624) matched a Pass the Hash pattern: an NTLM network logon with KeyLength 0, or a type 9 (NewCredentials) logon created by seclogo.
en.what_it_detects: 4624 events matching either of two conditions: LogonType 3 with LogonProcessName NtLmSsp, SubjectUserSid S-1-0-0 and KeyLength 0; or LogonType 9 with LogonProcessName seclogo. TargetUserName ANONYMOUS LOGON is excluded.
en.why_it_matters: In Pass the Hash (ATT&CK T1550.002), an attacker logs on with a stolen NTLM hash instead of the password and moves laterally. Tools that inject hashes often create type 9 seclogo sessions.
triage_steps: Identify the variant: LogonType 3 (inbound logon on the target host) or LogonType 9 (NewCredentials logon on the source host).
For type 3, check TargetUserName, TargetDomainName, IpAddress and WorkstationName. Confirm that this account normally connects from that source machine.
For type 9, check SubjectUserName, TargetOutboundUserName and ProcessName. Decide whether someone deliberately ran runas /netonly or credentials were injected.
On the source host, search 4688 or Sysmon within +/- 15 minutes for runas.exe, credential-dumping tools and access to lsass.exe (Sysmon 10).
On the target host, correlate on the same TargetLogonId: 4672 (special privileges), 5140/5145 (share access), 7045 (new services) and 4688.
Pivot on the account and IpAddress to look for NTLM logons to several hosts or earlier 4625 failures.
Check earlier alerts for the same account and host, and ask the owner whether an approved admin task was running.
false_positives: Administrators using runas /netonly or management consoles with alternate credentials (LogonType 9).
Inventory, monitoring or deployment tools that authenticate over NTLM to many hosts.
Legacy applications or services that only use NTLM and produce network logons with KeyLength 0.
response_steps: Before acting, confirm with the account owner and IT whether the activity was legitimate.
If it is malicious, isolate the source host through EDR and restrict the affected account.
Reset the password of the compromised account and of any privileged accounts that were logged on to the source, then revoke their sessions.
Hunt for persistence and lateral movement on target hosts (services, scheduled tasks, new binaries). Preserve evidence before removing anything.
To reduce exposure, restrict NTLM, deploy LAPS, add privileged accounts to Protected Users and enable Credential Guard.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits because the pattern matches Pass the Hash, but runas /netonly and legitimate NTLM also produce it, so context is needed to confirm.

positive.description: Inbound NTLM network logon with KeyLength 0 and a null subject SID, for a domain admin connecting from a workstation
Type 9 NewCredentials logon created by seclogo, as produced by runas /netonly or hash injection

negative.description: Anonymous NTLM null-session logon with KeyLength 0, excluded by the ANONYMOUS LOGON filter
Normal NTLM network logon with a 128-bit session key, so KeyLength does not match
